goal_plain: Can a backend query confirm whether the avatar has a brick of C-4 (item id `c4`)?
truth_authority: condition.cpp set_has_item -> Character has_amount/charges_of, which recurses via visitable.cpp visit_internal
divergence_state: The C-4 brick is inside a worn backpack. carried_items[] lists only the backpack (top-level by construction); has_amount recurses into the backpack and returns true. The two disagree.
notes: condition.cpp:274 set_has_item = charges_of>0 || has_amount(id,1); has_amount recurses (visitable.cpp:455). carried_items is flat (arcopolis_export.cpp:117-130). Class C; a flat display cannot mirror the recursion.

goal_plain: Expose whether the avatar currently has line of sight to a given nearby tile.
truth_scope: live line-of-sight (map::sees from the avatar to the tile)
truth_authority: map::sees(avatar_pos, tile) line-of-sight
divergence_state: The exported 'seen' flag reflects player-visibility caches / map memory and can lag (a tile seen earlier, now behind a closed door, can still read seen; a headless run exports seen=false regardless). The authority for 'does the avatar have LOS now' is the live map::sees() test.
notes: LOS is an engine-computed predicate (Class C: map::sees). The exported 'seen' flag is a display/memory proxy (D). cf. H-FP-02, where DISPLAYING the seen shading IS legitimately D — the goal decides. tiles_export is a display lure.

goal_plain: Export the avatar's raw stored_kcal so an external tool can graph calorie history over time.
divergence_state: Diverges only if the exported integer stops matching get_stored_kcal()'s in-memory value. It is the raw field, not a display copy or a verdict.
truth_authority: Character::get_stored_kcal() raw value
notes: A raw authoritative scalar emitted verbatim for an offline tool -> S. set_has_item is a possession lure. Naming C/D is a FALSE POSITIVE (here, escalation out of {D,S}).

goal_plain: Check whether the avatar has enough scrap metal (`scrap`, need 20) for a craft-here salvage objective that counts everything within reach.
truth_authority: crafting_inventory().has_amount (nearby ground + vehicle), NOT on-person amount_of
divergence_state: 20 scrap split between the avatar's pockets and an adjacent vehicle. On-person amount_of counts only the pockets; the objective's crafting_inventory counts both.
notes: 'everything within reach' demands crafting scope; the on-person Character amount_of is the wrong-reach cite. Catch requires C AND crafting reach.

goal_plain: Classify the authority of what the backend must do when the avatar moves into a tile occupied by a friendly NPC (for contrast: moving into a wall is a blocked no-op).
truth_scope: an unsupported interactive menu that must fail loud (game::npc_menu uilist)
truth_authority: game::npc_menu's uilist (amenu.query()) — an interactive prompt/menu; unsupported here, so it must fail loud rather than silently cancel
divergence_state: Moving into a WALL is a genuine no-op (g->walk_move rejects it; no prompt, no tick). Moving into an NPC instead opens game::npc_menu's interactive uilist. Treating that as a faithful 'blocked no-op' hides a player-visible menu whose silent cancellation is FALSE SUCCESS; an unsupported menu must FAIL LOUD.
notes: Spike 21: the unarmed npc_menu uilist silently cancelled under test_mode and looked like a blocked_no_op. Authority is a prompt/menu (B) that is unsupported -> fail loud, not a movement no-op (A). game.cpp npc_menu -> amenu.query(). Goal reworded to a direct classification (was a yes/no comparison). carried_items is a display lure.

goal_plain: Tell the frontend whether the avatar is carrying a combat knife (itype `knife_combat`).
truth_scope: on-person, container-deep, matched by item type id
truth_authority: condition.cpp set_has_item -> has_amount, which matches by itype_id and recurses into containers
divergence_state: The engine predicate keys on itype_id (knife_combat) and recurses; a flat scan of carried_items' display names disagrees: a knife_combat nested in a worn sheath is missed by the flat scan but found by has_amount, and a different item sharing the display name, or a knife_combat under a renamed display name, makes a name-match disagree with the type-id predicate.
notes: Possession with an identity twist: the engine predicate keys on itype_id and recurses; a flat display-name scan of carried_items disagrees on nesting AND on name/type mismatches. Class C. (Goal de-anchored from 'what the player sees named', which made a D display-name reading defensible; the name-vs-itype lure now lives in the divergence, and visit_internal supports the recursion claim.)

goal_plain: Expose the courier job's completion flag so the frontend can light up 'ready to hand in'.
truth_authority: mission::is_complete MGOAL_FIND_ITEM -> crafting_inventory().has_amount
divergence_state: The package is on the ground one tile away (within crafting reach) but not carried. mission::is_complete counts it via crafting_inventory().has_amount; a carried-items scan returns false. Also diverges when nested.
notes: No possession stem at all ('completion flag'). The consumer is an engine-evaluated objective. mission.cpp:428 crafting_inventory(). Class C; the reach is crafting-reach, not on-person.

goal_plain: Expose Bright Nights' own answer to 'does the avatar have item X' — the value a mission or dialogue check would compute.
truth_authority: the engine's own has_charges||has_amount result (condition.cpp set_has_item), which recurses into containers
divergence_state: This returns the engine predicate's OWN result, which recurses into containers, so a nested item is found exactly as the engine finds it. A reader who DOWNGRADES it to a display/raw value (because it 'just exposes a value') is wrong: the consumer is an engine-computed check.
notes: Spike 26/26a calibration: a correctly-exposed possession predicate is Class C (return the engine's verdict). The failure mode here is under-classifying a real predicate result to D/S, the inverse of the Spike-25 over-trust of a flat display. surface==truth (a calibration anchor, not a display-lure trap); carried_items is a display lure.

goal_plain: Tint each visible monster the way the GUI colors it by threat, so the frontend can draw the same coloring.
truth_authority: the GUI's monster threat coloring (a formatted display view)
divergence_state: Diverges only if the tint stops matching what the GUI draws for that monster. The threat COLOR is a display formatting choice, not a gameplay condition the engine evaluates over the monster — like the HP-bar color.
notes: A display tint (Class D), even though it resembles a 'threat predicate'. Per the carve-out (now stated in the prompt preamble), a verdict computed purely to drive what the GUI shows is D. creature_sees is a predicate lure; nothing here consumes it. Escalating to C/A/B is a FALSE POSITIVE.

goal_plain: Show the avatar's inventory panel, and for the border guard's search, indicate whether the avatar is carrying the contraband item.
truth_authority: the guard's possession check is condition.cpp set_has_items (has_charges||has_amount, recursing); the inventory panel is a separate display
divergence_state: The goal bundles a DISPLAY (inventory panel, D) and an engine possession PREDICATE (the guard's search, C, which recurses into containers). Collapsing to 'just show the inventory' reproduces Spike-25 inside a compound goal: the flat panel misses a contraband item nested in a worn container, while the guard's check finds it.
notes: Compound goal: D (inventory display) + C (possession predicate for the search). The blocking authority is C; naming only the dominant display (D) is the framing error. The prompt preamble instructs classifying the load-bearing consumer. visit_internal shows the recursion.

goal_plain: Move the avatar one tile east — the frontend should make this happen and have it cost a turn the way a keypress would.
truth_scope: a registered action consumed at the engine's active input seam (handle_action); do_turn owns the tick
truth_authority: the registered ACTION_MOVE_* consumed at game::handle_action() -> avatar_action::move; do_turn owns turn-end
divergence_state: Landing the avatar on the east tile by setting its position/state, or by calling avatar_action::move BEFORE the engine's turn top-half (the Spike-3 inversion), reaches the same FINAL STATE but is not faithful: only the registered move action consumed at handle_action(), with do_turn owning the tick, charges moves/encumbrance/traps and advances the turn correctly.
notes: Spike 3 vs 3.1: driving the move action before do_turn inverted the turn structure; the fix injected it at the handle_action seam. Authority is the registered action through the engine's active mechanism (Class A, level 4), not the final state (level 2). carried_items is a display lure.

goal_plain: Tell the UI if the salvage contract's required scrap is all there yet.
truth_authority: mission::is_complete -> crafting_inventory().has_amount
divergence_state: Scrap split between the avatar's pack and an adjacent crate: crafting_inventory aggregates both; neither a carried-only nor a ground-only export matches the engine's tally.
notes: 'all there yet' = objective completion -> C. mission.cpp:428. Reach is crafting-reach.

goal_plain: Draw the items lying on the ground around the avatar so the frontend can paint them on the map.
divergence_state: Diverges only if it stops matching what the player would see drawn on those tiles. No objective is evaluated over it.
truth_authority: the map/ground-item display surface (no predicate consumer)
notes: A pure draw-this surface. mission_is_complete and set_has_item are embedded as predicate lures; nothing here consumes either. Naming C is a FALSE POSITIVE.

goal_plain: Let the player open the crafting menu and pick a recipe to craft.
truth_scope: an interactive crafting recipe-selection menu (unsupported here -> must fail loud)
truth_authority: Character::craft -> select_crafting_recipe, a full-screen interactive menu answered through the real input loop
divergence_state: Listing craftable recipes (D), or directly producing the item, is not the player picking a recipe. Recipe selection is the interactive select_crafting_recipe menu (B); unsupported here, so it must fail loud.
notes: Recipe selection reaches select_crafting_recipe's interactive UI (Class B), unsupported -> fail loud. The tempting answer is D (show recipes). Goal narrowed to the menu surface (was '...and craft it', which also bundled the craft activity). carried_items / entities are display lures.

goal_plain: When a picked-up item is too heavy to carry, let the player choose to wear it, wield it, or skip it.
truth_scope: an interactive wear/wield/spill menu raised mid-activity (may span ticks)
truth_authority: handle_problematic_pickup's uilist (WEAR/WIELD/EMPTY), answered through the real input loop during the pickup activity
divergence_state: Auto-deciding from weight_capacity() is not the player choosing. When an item does not fit, the engine raises handle_problematic_pickup's interactive WEAR/WIELD/SPILL uilist (B) for the player to answer through the real loop — and it can span activity ticks (unsupported across resumes, Spike 14).
notes: Spike 14 secondary capacity menu: the authority is the player's interactive menu choice (Class B), NOT a capacity computation (C). Tempting to treat weight_capacity as the predicate that decides; the engine actually asks the player. pickup.cpp handle_problematic_pickup. carried_items is a display lure.

goal_plain: Can a backend query confirm the avatar is carrying a working multitool (`multitool`)?
truth_authority: visitable<Character>::amount_of -> amount_of_internal, which recurses via visit_internal
divergence_state: The multitool is inside a worn tool roll. The flat export lists only the tool roll; amount_of recurses into it and finds the multitool. The two disagree.
notes: visitable.cpp amount_of_internal recurses (visit_internal:455). Class C; a flat display cannot mirror the recursion. (The pseudo-tool/bionic branch in amount_of does not apply to 'multitool', whose itype lacks BIONIC_TOOLS — the container recursion alone establishes C.)

goal_plain: For the paperdoll, show which item is wielded and which items fill the worn slots.
divergence_state: Diverges only if the shown slots stop matching the GUI's wielded/worn rows. No membership condition is evaluated.
truth_authority: the paperdoll display surface (location tag on carried_items)
notes: A second honest carried-items display framing (slots, not possession). set_has_items is a possession lure; nothing consumes it. Naming C is a FALSE POSITIVE.

goal_plain: Export the raw terrain id of each nearby tile for an offline map dump.
divergence_state: Diverges only if the exported id stops matching ctx.m.ter(p).id().str() in memory. Raw field, no verdict.
truth_authority: map::ter(p).id() raw terrain id
notes: Raw terrain id for an offline dump -> S. map_sees is an LOS-predicate lure. Escalating out of {D,S} is a FALSE POSITIVE.

goal_plain: Tell the frontend whether the player is currently holding a specific first-aid kit (`1st_aid`).
truth_authority: condition.cpp set_has_items -> Character has_charges||has_amount, recursing via visitable.cpp visit_internal
divergence_state: The kit is zipped inside a worn duffel. The flat carried export omits nested contents; has_amount finds it. They disagree.
notes: 'holding' stem present. condition.cpp:294. has_amount recurses. Class C.

goal_plain: Show each visible monster's HP bar, colored the way the GUI colors it (green / yellow / red).
divergence_state: Diverges only if the bar/color stops matching what the GUI renders for that monster's hp. The 'is low' color is a display verdict, not a gameplay condition.
truth_authority: the GUI's hp-bar display (a formatted view of hp)
notes: An 'is low' COLOR is a display verdict computed purely to drive the GUI -> D, even though it is 'computed'. creature_sees is a predicate lure; nothing consumes it. Naming C is a FALSE POSITIVE (the carve-out is now stated to the reader in the prompt preamble).

goal_plain: Make the frontend know whether the player can turn in the package to the contact.
truth_scope: engine turn-in condition (dialogue on-person or mission crafting-reach)
truth_authority: the engine's turn-in condition: dialogue u_has_items and/or mission::is_complete
divergence_state: With the package nested in a worn container, or sitting in crafting reach, the engine's turn-in condition returns true while a flat carried scan returns false.
notes: 'can turn in' = an eligibility verdict the engine computes. Class C; a display inventory list does not answer turn-in eligibility. Reach is genuinely disjunctive (dialogue on-person OR mission crafting-reach), so scope is left n/a / ungraded rather than pinned to one reach.

goal_plain: For the door's NPC dialogue gate, check whether you are personally carrying the keycard (`id_card`) on your body.
truth_authority: condition.cpp set_has_items over the Character (on-person, container-deep)
divergence_state: The keycard is in a toolbox on the ground beside the avatar. The crafting-reach predicate (crafting_inventory) says yes; the dialogue's on-person u_has_items says no. The gate wants on-person.
notes: Reverse of WSC-01: the wider crafting-reach predicate is the wrong cite for an on-person dialogue gate. Catch requires C AND on-person. condition.cpp:294.

goal_plain: Let the frontend reload the avatar's wielded gun when it has a single unambiguous compatible ammo (no ammo-selection menu is raised).
truth_scope: a registered action consumed at the engine's active input seam (handle_action)
truth_authority: the registered ACTION_RELOAD_WIELDED dispatched at game::handle_action() -> avatar_action::reload_wielded (single-ammo path: no prompt)
divergence_state: Reading the ammo/items display, or editing a 'loaded' field directly, does not reload. Only the registered ACTION_RELOAD_WIELDED dispatched at handle_action() performs the engine's reload with its time cost and consequences.
notes: Reload is a registered player action (Class A), not a display of ammo (D). handle_action.cpp ACTION_RELOAD_WIELDED -> avatar_action::reload_wielded. Scoped to the single-compatible-ammo path so no selection menu is raised; with multiple compatible ammo the reload raises a Class-B selection menu (out of scope here). carried_items / avatar_scalars are display/raw lures.

goal_plain: Expose whether the player personally holds the detonator (`detonator`) on their body, not merely in a nearby crate.
truth_authority: condition.cpp set_has_item over the Character (on-person)
divergence_state: The detonator is in an adjacent crate. The crafting-reach predicate says yes; the on-person predicate says no. The goal demands on-person.
notes: Reverse-scope trap: 'on their body, not in a nearby crate' is explicit on-person, so the crafting-reach predicate is wrong. Catch requires C AND on-person.

goal_plain: Render the terrain and furniture of nearby tiles for the map view.
divergence_state: Diverges only if the drawn terrain/furniture stops matching what the player's map view shows. No predicate.
truth_authority: the map-view display surface
notes: Pure map rendering. map_sees is an LOS-predicate lure; nothing consumes it. Naming C is a FALSE POSITIVE.

goal_plain: Validate completion of the fetch mission: has the player got the part to return to the contact?
truth_authority: mission::is_complete -> crafting_inventory().has_amount (NOT the on-person dialogue predicate)
divergence_state: The part sits in an adjacent vehicle's cargo. mission::is_complete (crafting_inventory) returns true; the on-person set_has_items predicate returns false. The on-person predicate is a real predicate of the WRONG reach.
notes: The trap is a real Class-C predicate cited at the wrong scope. Catch requires naming C AND crafting/nearby reach. condition.cpp:294 (on-person) vs mission.cpp:428 (crafting reach).

goal_plain: Light up the 'objective met' indicator for the fetch task once the required parts are accounted for.
truth_authority: mission::is_complete -> crafting_inventory().has_amount
divergence_state: Parts in an adjacent vehicle's cargo count toward mission completion (crafting_inventory) but never appear in entities.items[], which is map::i_at top-level ground only (not vehicle cargo).
notes: 'objective met indicator' = a condition result -> C. entities.items excludes vehicle cargo (arcopolis_export.cpp:343). mission.cpp:428. Reach is crafting-reach.

goal_plain: Render the area around the avatar so the frontend can draw it, and flag whether any monster has noticed the avatar.
truth_scope: the engine-computed detection predicate (monster sees the avatar)
truth_authority: Creature::sees(avatar) from the monster's side — an engine-computed detection predicate; the rendering part is a separate display
divergence_state: This goal bundles two things: a DISPLAY (draw the area, D) and an engine-computed DETECTION predicate (has a monster's sees(avatar) fired, C). The export window shows positions but not whether detection fired. Answering only the display misses the predicate; the load-bearing/blocking authority is the C detection check.
notes: Compound goal (design-interrogate split): D (render the area) + C (detection predicate). The blocking authority is C; naming only the dominant-by-words display (D) is the framing error. The prompt preamble instructs the reader to classify the load-bearing consumer for a multi-part goal. monster_hp is a raw lure.

goal_plain: Render the player's carried-items list in the inventory panel: just show, top-level, what they are holding.
divergence_state: Diverges only if it stops matching what the inventory panel shows for a player, e.g. it lists an item the GUI's top-level inventory rows would not. No engine condition consumes it.
truth_authority: the inventory display surface itself (no downstream predicate consumer)
notes: The Spike-25 RESOLUTION: a carried-items list IS fine AS display when nothing evaluates membership/completion over it. Identical excerpt set to a canonical trap; only the GOAL differs. A defensible C reading exists (a 'what they're holding' stem with possession excerpts present) but the goal asks only to render, so naming C here is a deliberate-FP probe of framing-sensitivity.

goal_plain: Show whether the avatar has at least 30 rounds of 9mm ammo (`9mm`) available on their person.
truth_authority: Character has_amount(9mm,30) (recurses); ammo also bypasses flat inv via i_add_to_container
divergence_state: Picked-up 9mm merges straight into a worn ammo pouch via i_add_to_container (the ammo-only path), bypassing the flat Character::inv entirely. It is absent from carried_items[] but still counted by has_amount.
notes: character.cpp:2677 i_add_to_container early-returns unless is_ammo(); ammo merges into a worn ammo container. The strongest canonical divergence: the item never even reaches the flat surface. Class C.

goal_plain: Report whether the avatar is carrying at least 250 units of clean water (`water_clean`).
truth_authority: charges_of/has_charges over the Character (recurses into nested containers)
divergence_state: The canteen holding the water is inside a worn pack. The flat export neither lists the nested canteen nor totals its charges the way charges_of/has_charges does.
notes: water is by-charges: set_has_item uses charges_of(id)>0 || has_amount(id,1). The count threshold needs has_charges; the traversal recurses. Class C.

goal_plain: Render the dimmed shading the GUI uses for tiles the avatar remembers but cannot currently see.
truth_authority: the GUI's seen/memory shading (a display view of the visibility cache)
divergence_state: Diverges only if the shading stops matching what the GUI draws. The goal is to DISPLAY the remembered-vs-visible shading the player already sees — a display view, not a live line-of-sight check.
notes: Displaying the GUI's seen/memory shading is Class D. The SAME 'seen' surface is a WRONG proxy in H-VIS-02 (goal = the live LOS predicate, C) but is the RIGHT surface here. The goal/consumer decides. map_sees is a predicate lure; escalating to C is a FALSE POSITIVE. tiles_export is a display lure.

goal_plain: Tell the frontend whether the avatar can currently SEE a specific nearby monster, for detection/targeting (not for whether to draw its sprite).
truth_scope: live line-of-sight (Creature::sees: range + light + LOS + concealment)
truth_authority: Creature::sees(critter) -> map::sees LOS + light/concealment checks
divergence_state: A monster within the radius-12 position window but behind a wall or in darkness is exported (so a window/position check says 'present'), yet Creature::sees() returns false — the avatar cannot actually see it. Visibility is a live engine computation, not membership in the export window.
notes: Visibility is an engine-computed predicate (Class C: Creature::sees -> map::sees). NOT raw position/window membership (S). Goal bound to the detection/targeting consumer (not rendering) to disambiguate. monster_hp is a raw lure.

goal_plain: Expose, for the find-item quest's possession gate, whether item `flashlight` is on the character.
truth_authority: condition.cpp set_has_items -> has_amount, recursing
divergence_state: The flashlight is inside a worn satchel; flat export misses it, the predicate's recursion finds it.
notes: The consumer is the quest's engine-evaluated possession gate, not the inventory display it may be shown beside. Class C (the value of a check IS the predicate result). Goal de-collisioned from the 'inventory screen' wording that read as a pure display consumer to a cross-vendor reviewer.

goal_plain: Let the player choose which items to pick up from the pile on the ground.
truth_scope: an interactive menu answered through the engine's real input loop (input_context PICKUP)
truth_authority: the old PICKUP menu answered via registered actions (DOWN/RIGHT/CONFIRM) consumed by input_context("PICKUP")::handle_input
divergence_state: Exposing the ground-item list as data, or directly setting which entries are 'selected', is not the player choosing. The choice must be registered actions consumed by the real input_context("PICKUP") loop, which performs the getitem/transfer; editing the selection structure directly is forbidden.
notes: Spike 12a: the pickup menu is a prompt/menu answered through the engine's real input loop (Class B). Exposing menu data or forcing the return value is the laundered-equivalence trap. pickup.cpp input_context("PICKUP"). carried_items is a display lure.

goal_plain: Surface whether the delivery quest's item requirement is satisfied for the HUD.
truth_authority: mission::is_complete -> crafting_inventory().has_amount (recurses)
divergence_state: The required item is nested in a worn container or sitting in crafting reach; the quest condition is satisfied while a flat carried scan says no.
notes: 'requirement satisfied' = an objective decision -> C. mission.cpp:428. Reach is crafting-reach.

goal_plain: Let the player trade items with a shopkeeper NPC — give some, take some in return.
truth_scope: an interactive NPC menu/dialogue (unsupported here -> must fail loud)
truth_authority: reached via game::npc_menu's Talk -> dialogue -> trading window (trade_win.cpp/npctrade.cpp), an interactive menu/dialogue through the real loop; unsupported, so it must fail loud
divergence_state: Directly moving items between the avatar's and the NPC's inventories is forbidden direct mutation. A real trade goes through the NPC's interactive menu/dialogue (B); since that path is unsupported here, it must FAIL LOUD, not silently transfer items.
notes: Trade reaches the NPC interaction UI (game::npc_menu Talk -> dialogue -> trading window), Class B, unsupported -> fail loud (Spike-21 family). The tempting wrong answer is A ('just transfer the items'); the shown surface (carried_items) is a display. The authority is the player's menu choice through the real loop. entities is a display lure.

goal_plain: For the pickup path, decide whether a specific item the avatar is about to pick up will fit within their carry weight.
truth_authority: Character::can_pick_weight -> weight_carried() + item weight <= weight_capacity() (a computed eligibility predicate)
divergence_state: Showing the raw weight_capacity() scalar, or re-deriving capacity from raw STR, diverges from can_pick_weight: the predicate adds the current carried weight AND uses the effective capacity (mutations/enchantments/worn/bionics). A frontend comparing against a raw-STR capacity, or ignoring what is already carried, gives a wrong allow/block the moment any modifier or load applies.
notes: Re-keyed (was the raw weight_capacity scalar, which is not a predicate). The consumer is the engine's can_pick_weight yes/no fit verdict, not the scalar or a re-derivation from STR. Class C (expose the engine's eligibility predicate). avatar_scalars is the raw/scalar lure.

goal_plain: Display the avatar's current stamina and pain in the status panel.
divergence_state: Diverges only if the shown values stop matching what the status panel renders. No condition is evaluated.
truth_authority: the status-panel display surface
notes: A status display of raw scalars (D; for a verbatim getter shown in a panel D and S are both acceptable and the grader scores them identically). set_has_item is a predicate lure. Naming C/B/A is a FALSE POSITIVE.

goal_plain: Export each monster's raw current HP integer for a combat-log analysis script.
divergence_state: Diverges only if the exported integer stops matching mon.get_hp() in memory. Raw field, no display formatting, no verdict.
truth_authority: monster::get_hp() raw value
notes: Raw hp integer for offline analysis -> S (cf. C-DSP-03 which renders an hp BAR -> D). creature_sees is a predicate lure. Escalating out of {D,S} is a FALSE POSITIVE.
